7. Cubicle (c), wall W with the high rectangular splayed window open onto the Alley of Thesmos: the remains of the decorative phase of the III style.
6. Cubicle (c), wall S, section O: A diamond can be seen in the red side panel. III style.
8. Cubicle (c), wall O, section S: medallion in the red panel of the middle area.
9. Triclinium (e): the remains of the cocciopesto floor plastered red.  79 N57841
11. Triclinium (e), N wall, detail of fig. Previous: Of the medallion with bust that was in the center of the wall, only the deeply engraved guide circle can now be distinguished.

10. Triclinium (e), wall N: preserves the remains of a simple decoration with a white background that Mau (A. Mau, in Bd, 1882, pp. 218-219) attributes to the III style. The room is lit by the door to the atrium and the tall, narrow window visible in the photograph, at ceiling level, overlooking the garden (i) of the complex of IX 7, 2122. Above the plinth, which bears the very simple ornamentation with splashes of black and red, the panels of the middle area are separated by narrow compartments with twisted candelabra, while at the end are stretched garlands.
12. Triclinium (e), wall E: remains of a fresco of the III style; the jambs are made of limestone blocks alternating with two rows of bricks.
13. Triclinium (e), wall W with recessed for the bed and remains of a fresco of the III style.
14. Triclinium (e), W wall, section N: vignette with bird. III style.

15. The wall O of the wardrobe (f), plastered in red, retains the holes for the shelves that supported the shelves; on the left you can see the S wall, restored (A. Mau, in BdI, 1883, p- 75) after the earthquake of 62 and still without plaster.

16. The peristyle (g) seen from S: on the right the yellow-plastered columns support the arched entablature; the columns of the O portico, with tufelli alternating with two brick recurrences, are instead devoid of plaster, like the one in the N-W corner; The difference in the finish of the porticoes is attributed to the consequences of an earthquake, that of 62 in the reports of the time of the excavation, or a subsequent one according to more recent hypotheses (cf. Archaologie und Seismologie, passim). The decoration of the peristyle was completed by the numerous oscilla found here and in the adjacent rooms (Dwyer1982, cited in bibl.).  '79 N57840

17. Peristyle (g), overall view from S-W: the old photograph shows the infill of the door that previously led from here to the tablinum (0) of House IX 7, 24-25; on the back walls of the arcades, before the reconstruction of the tetreti

18. Peristyle (g), portico E, wall E, section N: red floor and moulded stucco cornice. Materials and technique are those of the first style decorations, but here as in other rooms of the house they could be reproductions or imitations.
19. In the NE corner of the peristyle (g) the remains of the red plane with the moulded cornice are preserved.

20. Peristyle (g), portico E with arched entablature; the masonry base in the foreground was painted in imitation marble (II style) and supported a statue-fountain depicting a cupid with a mask of Pan (cf. Dwyer 1982, tav. XXX, fig. 115).

21. Peristyle (g): on the S wall of the S portico you can read the signs of one of the many construction changes attested in this area: the plaster in use in 79 covered the plaster of a previous decorative phase, which in turn covered the infill of a door existing here.
22. Lava millstone and fluted travertine support, which supported a bronze statue-fountain depicting a cupid with dolphin (cf. Dwyer 1982, tav. XXX, fig. 114).
23. The circular grey marble basin received water from the bronze statue-fountain, whose duct passed through the masonry base behind.
24. In the peristyle, the mouth of the terracotta cistern was covered with white stucco and subsequently walled up.
25. Room (h): square and circular tiles in breccia are inserted in the cocciopesto floor.

26. Room (h), wall N. Of the fourth style decoration, only colours and partitions can still be distinguished: the plinth is black, the middle area has a yellow central panel and red side panels, separated by blue compartments.

27. The decoration of the room (h) was not very demanding, as evidenced by the lack of figurative paintings and the presence, in the centre of the N wall, of a simple vignette with a rampant griffin. IV style. 79 N57829
28. Room (h), wall E: the plinth was black decorated with plants, the middle area has a red panel in the center and yellow side panels, separated by blue compartments containing candelabra. IV style.
29. Room (h), S wall with the door open to the peristyle (g): remains of a fresco of the IV style.

30. Room (h), wall W with opus mixtum masonry with bricks and fresco of the fourth style: black plinth with plants and middle area with red and yellow panels. From this room one passed, through a door that was later closed, into the courtyard (i) of House IX 7, 21-22.
31. Room (h), O wall, S section: vignette with swan in the middle area. IV style. '79 N57830
32. Room (i): in the papier-mâché floor — older than the wall decoration (cf. Partridge, cited in bibl.) — flakes of travertine are scattered.
34. Room (i): the E section of the door towards the peristyle preserves, above the decoration described above, the red lunette bordered by a green band and moulded cornices.
33. Room (i), wall Na O of the door open to the peristyle (g). Fresco of the fourth style: red plinth; black hoof with plants; yellow middle area with carpet edge panel; upper red area.

35. Room (i), wall E with the high window opening onto the rear garden. The wall decoration belongs to the initial phase of the IV style and retains some elements typical of the previous decorative phase. The long wall is divided, on the side of the central aedicule, by two-tone panels; The compartments of the upper area are also two-tone, above which the decoration is concluded by the stucco molded frame, while the lunette is in rough plaster.

37. Room (i), wall E, section N: the strips with V-motifs that delimit the narrow red compartment with candelabra are in the tradition of the III style; On the side, the panel has black and red areas separated by a candelabra and adorned with vignettes. A high ovoli frame imitating bronze separates the middle and upper areas: here the bicolorism of the middle area returns, with the partition entrusted to a thyrsus arranged obliquely on which a garland is wrapped. On the black background is represented a low architecture with avant-corps and acroterial vases; molded stucco frame. IV style.
36. Room (i), wall E, section N: vignette with still life in the black side panel; The subject of the cartoon — the palm tree and a vase — alludes to victories in the gymnasium. IV style.

38. Room (i), wall E, central section: painting with Ares and Aphrodite, surrounded by cupids playing with the now harmless weapons of the god, an allusion to the power of love; The metaphor is already present in the
39. The picture in fig. previous in the reproduction by G. Discanno.
40. Room (i), wall E, section S: vignette with vase and clypeus in the black panel of the middle area. IV style.

41. Room (i), wall E, section S: compartment with a red background bordered by V-shaped strips and containing a candelabra, and black and red panel with vignettes and carpet borders; yellow frame with ovoli and upper area with a black and red panel divided by a thyrsus arranged obliquely around which a garland is wrapped; on the low architecture with foreparts a parrot and a cist rest; above the stucco moulded cornice is visible the rough plaster of the lunette. IV style.
42. Room (i), S wall —with fresco of the fourth style, restored with rough plaster in the W section.

43. Room (i), wall S, section E: in the middle area there is a red panel with carpet edges, to the side of which is a yellow compartment bordered by strips with V-motifs and containing a golden twisted candelabrum surmounted by the globe; The fantastic architecture of the upper area is surmounted by a 'grotesque' animal holding a garland. IV style. 79 N57802
44. Room (i), wall S, section E: in the black panel of the middle area there is a still life vignette depicting a palm tree and a vase, a prize for the games in the gymnasium. IV style.
45. Room (i), S wall, section E: architecture with cist and acroterial bird in the upper area. IV style.
46. Room (i), S wall: the painting in the centre of the wall depicted Dionysus and Ariadne. IV style.

47. G. Discanno's drawing introduces us to the iconography of the painting in fig. previous: Dionysus and his retinue find Ariadne, abandoned by Theseus on the beach of Naxos, here in the company of a winged figure identified as Nemesis, a figure often present in paintings that represent another moment in the same story, the one in which Ariadne, just awakened, sees Theseus' boat fleeing in the distance.
48. Room (i), S wall, central section: the arched garland at the top of the panel and the crowning of the aedicule. IV style.
49. Room (i), S wall, section O: vignette with bird in the black panel of the middle area. IV style.

50. Room (i), wall O: the decoration of the initial IV style was spread over the plaster of a previous decorative phase, visible in the gaps of the subsequent decoration. Above the moulded frame in white stucco, the wall is finished with rough plaster.
51. The wall of fig. previous in the reproduction published by Niccolini.
52. Room (i), wall O, section S: black panel with vignette with still life ('agonistic' vases, palm and clypeus). IV style.
53. Room (i), wall O, section S: vignette with a swan in the red panel of the middle area. IV style.

54. Room (i), wall O: the painting, of unidentified iconography (Adonis leaves for the hunt on horseback accompanied by a figure in ' Persian guise?: cf. B. Servais-Soyes, in LIMC, I, p. 226, n. 30, s.wv. Adonis).
55. Room (i), wall W, central section: the aedicule is supported by gilded twisted candelabra and has a semi-lunar tympanum with acroterial palmettes. IV style. '79 N57807
56. Room (i), wall O, section N: panel with vignette with bird and carpet edges, ovoli frame and, in the upper area, a garland wrapped around a thyrsus. IV style.
57. Room (i), wall W, section N: vignette with still life (vase, palm tree and circle). IV style.
58. Room (k): the remains of the fourth style decoration are still legible, with a middle area with red panels separated by narrow yellow compartments. 79 N57853
59. Room (k), SW corner with the staircase (n) and the illegible remains of the IV style decoration.
60. Room (k), wall O, section N: the decoration of the fourth style — spread over a layer of preparation made up of large shards — is now illegible. 79 N57857
61. Room (1): cocciopesto floor in which travertine flakes are scattered.

62. Room (1): the N wall has almost completely lost the decoration of the IV style which, above a red plinth, had a white middle and upper area. In the center of the central panel was the painting reproduced in fig. In the following areas, in the side panels were vignettes with attributes of divinities, the dividing compartments were crossed by candelabra.
63. The painting with Poseidon and Amymone, now unrecognizable on the wall in fig. reproduced here from a drawing from the archive of the German Archaeological Institute (G. Discanno).
64. Room (Il), N wall, central section: garland in the upper white area. IV style. 79 N57846
65. Room (1), N wall, central section: upper area with archaistic figure within a garland. IV style.
66. Room (1), wall E with an arched door, walled up and covered with the decoration of the fourth style, which led into the area that now belongs to House IX 7, 25.

67. On the wall reproduced in fig. previous was the painting with Ariadne handing Theseus the thread that will help him get out of the labyrinth (here reproduced from a drawing by G. Discanno, DAIR archive), sog860
68. Room (1), S wall with remains of a fresco of the fourth style. '79 N57844
69. Room (1), wall W with the door open to the peristyle (g): above the decoration of the fourth style is preserved the stucco frame with lotuses.

70. The theme of the meeting of Ariadne and Dionysus, already seen on the back wall of room (i) (see fig. 47) also returns in room (1): between the two figures, Theseus' ship is visible in the distance (from a drawing by G. Discanno, DAIR archive).
71. Room (I), wall W, section N: stucco frame with 'table' surmounted by lotuses. '79 N57847
72. The masonry counter in the large kitchen (p).

73. Cubicle (r), wall O with rectangular splayed window. The presence of a decoration of the type of those of the first style inside the recess for the bed, normally absent in the cubicles set up in the Republican age, is surprising here: it must have been an imitation, as Mau had already supposed (A. Mau, in BdI, 1882, p.

74. Triclinium (s): room with a false vault roof, and 'anomalous' style IV decoration: the black plinth sprinkled with yellow is higher than usual; the white middle area has panels bordered by red bands and separated by narrow compartments with candelabras; in the upper area are architectures. 79 N57851

75. Triclinium (s), S wall with recess for the bed — in which the IV style decoration with a white background with panels bordered by red bands has been better preserved — and a window that takes light from the courtyard (u) (which is also overlooked by House IX 7, 19). 79 N57866
76. Triclinium (s), wall W: remains of a fresco of the fourth style with a white background. 79 N57867
77. Cubicle (w), wall W with rectangular splayed window open onto Vicolo di Tesmo: the wall is covered with rough plaster.

1. Bottega (a), wall O: it has a functional cladding with the plinth — as is frequent in this type of cladding — higher than usual, with a red background and divided by yellow bands that form panels; in the upper area you do not recognize any partition.

2. Room (b): at the base of the wall there are rows of large limestone blocks — evidently reused — laid dry, above which, at the height of the window open onto the Via degli Augustali, there are rows of limestone blocks alternating with brick recurrences and a stretch of irregular limestone blocks. The wall was covered with red and yellow plaster, here almost completely collapsed but datable to the IV style, as shown in the photos in figs. and from the news of Mau (Mau, in BdI, 1882, p. 194: 'E painted simply and crudely in the last style with a yellow background. In the middle of each compartment there is a small picture representing on the same yellow background a bird pecking at some fruit').

3. Room (b), wall E with masonry in opus incert: red plinth; middle area with narrow central compartment, also red, crossed by candelabra and yellow side panels bordered by carpet edges; the upper area is red.
4. Room (b), S wall with the door open to the atrium (c) and masonry in opus incerta that preserves the remains of frescoes of the IV style: red plinth and middle area with yellow panels.
5. Room (b), wall O, section N: remains of fresco of the fourth style.
6. Atrium (c), wall O: below this small square niche, in the room that welcomes people entering the house, the lararium was painted.

7. From the S wall of the corridor leading to the latrine, the fragment representing Fortuna with the modium on her head, the rudder resting on the globe in the right and the cornucopia in the left, as well as, in smaller dimensions, a defecating male figure surmounted by two apotropaic snakes, above which is paintedINS. 7, 21-22

1. Workshop (a) with entrance at no. 24: view from the north, from the Via degli Augustali. The shop has a large opening on the street, which could be closed by wooden boards to be embedded in the lava threshold; A corner masonry counter occupies most of the available space, leaving a passage free about as wide as the

2. Workshop (a): the ornamentation of the cocciopesto floor, dotted with white tiles, suggests that the use of the room as a workshop is secondary and that when the floor, assignable to the phase of the first style, was made, the room had a residential function (a cubicle ?). The marble threshold in the foreground is however later.
3. Workshop (a): in the O wall there are two rectangular niches.
4. Atrium (2), N wall, section O: to the left of the hearth communicating with the workshop at no. 24 is a fourth-style decoration with a red background with carpet borders.

5. Atrium (2), wall O: in the masonry in opus incerta — covered with scarce remains of a fresco of the fourth style with a red background — there are large blocks of limestone; the jamb is made of limestone blocks alternating with two brick recourses.
6. Atrium (2), O wall, S section: red plinth and middle area with red panels with angular volutes. IV style.

7. Cubicle (b), floor: in the cocciopesto it is now very difficult to distinguish the space of the alcove (devoid of ornaments, on the right), from that of the antechamber (a dotted with crosses of white tesserae, on the left), separated by a simple row of white tesserae widely spaced. Like that of the workshop (a) (see fig. 2), the ornamentation can be assigned to the Republican age.
8. Cubicle (b): on wall E there are now illegible remains of frescoes, which Mau (cited in the bibl.) describes as having a yellow background and adorned with birds, assignable to the IV style.

9. Triclinium (1), N wall with recessed bed: the IV style decoration with a red background consists of a high red plinth with panels bordered by stretched garlands; in the right panel there was a painting with a landscape, now illegible. From Mau (Mau, in Bdi, 1882, p. 1977) we know that a rectangle containing fragments of marble marked the place of the table, and that the floor covering was better preserved [as in the tablinum (or) ?] in the area occupied by the beds. 79 N53174
10. Triclinium (1), detail of fig. Previous: The flowers that adorn the stretched garlands were stolen by an expert hand.

11. Triclinium (1): on the masonry in opus incerta, with jambs in opus mixed with reticulate and bricks, the decoration of the fourth style is preserved. The plinth, unusually high, is divided into panels containing squares; The coating of the upper area is no longer distinguishable.
12. Triclinium (l), S wall, section O: picture with bird in the red middle area. IV style.
14. Cubicle (m), wall E with recessed bed: remains of a simple decoration of the fourth style with a narrow central compartment with a red background and yellow side panels.
13. Triclinium (1), wall O: the fresco of the fourth style has a bipartite structure and large side panels bordered by carpet edges; the upper area is discolored.
15. Cubicle (m), S wall: remains of a fresco of the fourth style.
16. Cubicle (m), wall W, section S: remains of a fresco in the recess for the bed.

17. Tablinum (0), wall E: a large jamb in lava blocks and bricks leans against the masonry in opus incerte, covered with a first plaster (later abolished) and, later, by a decoration of the fourth style with a red background, while the upper area is in rough plaster. The room had a decorated cocciopesto floor.

18. Tablinum (0): the S wall — built after the separation from the adjoining House IX 7, 20 — has a red plinth; middle area with central square with a white background and red side panels, the upper area is in rough plaster (?).  At the center of the IV style decoration was a painting with a cupid in flight.  '79 N53179
19. Tablinum (o), wall W with the door of (n) and remains of a fresco of the fourth style: red plinth; red middle area with panels bordered by carpet edges.

20. Fauces (p): the S wall — built after the separation from House IX 7, 20 — bears on this side, as on the opposite side (cf. p. 837, fig. 17), the remains of a white plan and a molded cornice of the first style. 79 N53193

21. Room (q), wall S: also in this room — as in the rest of the house — the plinth is higher than usual and divided into panels (here with a yellow background, bordered by white and red bands and containing vignettes with animals or competitive vases).
22. Environment (q): detail of fig. Previous: Cartoon with bird. IV style.
23. Room (q): detail of fig. 21: vignette with still life with 'agonistic' vase. IV style.
24. Room (q), wall O: fresco of the fourth style with a high plinth with a yellow background surmounted by an upper area of rough plaster.

25. Corridor(s), W wall. Mau (cited in bibl.) assigns this decoration to the III style of candelabra; in the high red plinth there are panels separated by narrow compartments; A black frame marks the transition to the black middle area, adorned with vignettes with landscapes.

26. Viridarium (u), NW corner: the entrance to the peristyle of House IX 77, 20 is filled in and covered with plaster. The black pilasters that support the banded architrave, concluded by a moulded cornice and a red frieze, above which is a tiled roof, date back to the previous phase, which can be assigned to the first style. The space between the pilasters has been restored with rough plaster. 79 N53191
27. Viridarium (u): detail of fig. previous. 79 N53190

1. Façade with the entrance portal with jambs in blocks of Sarno limestone, surmounted by cubic capitals of tuff; the architrave was covered with stucco, the façade, in uncertain work, by a high plinth of rough plaster.

2. Façade: detail of the architrave of the entrance portal, made of Sarno limestone, of which part of a dentilled stucco cladding remains, to which a subsequent moulded cornice, also in stucco, with drip tray, has been superimposed.
3. Vestibule (1), N wall, section E: detail of a panel of the black middle area with carpet edges with two parallel lines.
4. Atrium (2), wall E in opus incert with edge in opus brick. The hoof and the middle area were red.
5. Atrium (2), S wall with a lararium niche in the W section. The plinth is discolored, the red middle area was articulated in panels with carpet edges. '79 N58606
6. Atrium (2), S wall, section O: detail of the lararium niche at the bottom of which was painted a dentilled frame surmounted by two-tone ashlars.

7. Room (a): the large triclinium that had the recess for the bed in the E wall, was transformed in the northern part into a kitchen with the construction of the counter that was leaning against the N-W corner, and in the southern part into a latrine; the walls were covered with simple white plaster.

caption_en: 8. Room (a), wall E: in the recess for the bed, present in section N, the remains of two black ashlars of the original decoration of the first style are preserved.

caption_en: 9. Room (a): in the S part, by inserting a dividing partition, the latrine was installed, also equipped with a O-shaped window. In the S wall there are holes for support beams, perhaps for a low floor.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 8, Property b, Room a

caption_en: 10. Cubicle (b): the function of the room, unchanged over time, is confirmed by the presence of the recess for the bed in wall E which, like wall N, retains traces of a layer of plaster tapped for the adhesion of the next white one.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 8, Property b, Room b

caption_en: 11. Tablinum (c): the cocciopesto floor denotes its belonging to the first style due to the presence in it of scattered white limestone flakes.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 8, Property b, Room c

caption_en: 12. Tablinum (c), N wall: the purplish red plinth is divided into panels with carpet edges with two parallel lines, surmounted by a peacock facing the centre, and separated by narrow compartments with plants. In the middle area, the yellow panels are separated by narrow architectural views. The upper area is discolored.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 8, Property b, Room c

caption_en: 13. Tablinum (c), wall E: the panels of the purplish red plinth are crossed by edges of carpet in semicircles, visible immediately to the right of the left compartment. The architectural glimpse that separates the left panel from the central one in the middle area still retains traces of the lower partition. On the S corner there was a pilaster of which you can barely see the mirrors.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 8, Property b, Room c

caption_en: 14. Tablinum (c): the W wall still retained some traces of colour in the compartments with plants on the sides of the plinth panel with a semicircular carpet border, and in the architectural glimpses of the middle area in which the gate and the coffered ceiling can be recognisable above the partition.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 8, Property b, Room c

caption_en: 15. Wardrobe (d) with holes for the supports of the shelves in the walls N, E and O plastered in white.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 8, Property b, Room d

caption_en: 16. Corridor (e), N wall: in the black plinth you can see the corollas of large flowers; a yellow molded frame separates it from the red middle area in which the red panels, with carpet edges with two parallel lines, are separated by a compartment crossed by a stretched garland.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 8, Property b, Room e

caption_en: 17. Cubicle (h), N wall, section O: in the upper area remains the floor surmounted by a very protruding frame that still retains the colors of the fake flowering alabaster, green, yellow and pink, of the first style decoration. The middle area was instead redone in the fourth style with a white background, with panels with carpet edges with two parallel red lines.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 8, Property b, Room h

caption_en: 18. Cubicle (h): in the decoration of the fourth style the plinth was white, the middle area of the same color, with three panels with carpet edges with two parallel lines, separated by narrow compartments. In the upper area there is the plan with the very protruding frame of the first style, the high white frieze followed again by a flat with a frame.

caption_en: 19. Cubicle (h), wall S: in section O there is the recess for the bed and, given the better state of preservation, it can be recognized that in the panel and in the compartment of the white plinth there are plants, while the compartment, which separates the panels in the middle area, is crossed by a stretched garland.

caption_en: 1. In the section of the façade between the shops at nos. l and 2 the presence of electoral inscriptions was identified under the layer of rough plaster that covered the previous plaster, recognizable here in the area of the gap near the metric pole.
2. Workshop at no. 2, room (1), N wall, section W of the door: discoloured plinth, but probably black, with a yellow reed gate, with fire flares.
3. Room (1), N wall, E section of the door: the plinth and the middle area are discolored, but in the latter there is a horizontal wreath, with a small square in the center. 79 N50077

4. Room (1), wall E: in the discolored plinth the reed gate can be distinguished; the middle area, divided into three narrow panels, had in the central one a small picture with a sacred landscape that has been removed; traces of the fading frieze with philosophers can be distinguished.

5. Room (1), wall E: the watercolour of the German Archaeological Institute reproduces the small picture (0.34 x 0.35) removed from the middle area. The description given by Mau himself (cited in bibl., p. 32), differs only in the detail of a base with three statues, which should be found to the right of the temple, whose entablature is

6. Room (1), wall E; detail of the frieze in Sikkard's drawing, kept in the German Archaeological Institute: a standing philosopher and a seated philosopher, identifiable as such by the himation wrapped around the body leaving the torso and right arm uncovered, are separated by a column and a tree that serves as a background.

7. Room (1), wall E; detail of the frieze in Sikkard's drawing kept in the German Archaeological Institute: a bearded philosopher stands, leaning on a stick and looks towards a younger character, seated near a column, unfolding a roll, raising his left.

8. Room (1), wall E; detail of the frieze in Sikkard's drawing kept in the German Archaeological Institute: a philosopher seated on klismòs, supports his head with his left, in a pensive attitude and looks downwards.

9. Room (1), wall E; detail of the frieze in Sikkard's drawing kept in the German Archaeological Institute: a standing philosopher with a bident looking towards two other characters seated on marble benches. The latter two are characterized by thick and dark hair, the other by a strong receding hairline that is accompanied by short and white hair.

10. Room (1), wall E; detail of the frieze in Sikkard's drawing kept in the German Archaeological Institute: bearded philosopher standing, with his head turned to the left, towards which he points to a young man standing near a column and some rocks on which another elderly personage sits, bearded and dressed in himdtion, like a philosopher or a man of letters, holding a scroll in his left. A tree with sparse leaves is the background.

11. Room (1), wall O: the picture (0.34 x 0.35) is reproduced in the watercolour of the German Archaeological Institute. In a wooded area, dominated by two high conical mountains, and which we must imagine Mediterranean due to the presence of palm trees, there is a tower with a colonnade at the top, near which there is a large tower. 8, 1 and 2
12. Room (1), wall O from the centre of which the small picture with the sacred landscape of fig. 11 was removed, completely removing the masonry. The discolored plinth has a reed gate. '79 N50074
13. Back room (2), wall O in uncertain work with a previous layer of plaster tapped to make the new one adhere to it now completely discolored. 79 N50076

1. Vestibule (1): the mosaic floor, made in the last decades of the city's life, as indicated by the size and straight arrangement of the tiles, presents, on the black field, a carpet with a white background with, in black, a dolphin and a sea griffin swimming to the left; the sea is rendered with short horizontal stretches, which give static to the scene. Triclinium (8), wall N: the repertoire exhibited in the decoration of this wall, entirely on a black background, which gives an impression of overall sobriety, despite the richness of the decorative details, leads back to that present on the walls of the portico of the Temple of Isis (VIII 7, 28: cf. vol. VIII, pp. 738 ff.), for which there is a certain date of reconstruction after the earthquake of 62 AD; For this reason, we can think of bringing the decoration of this room back to the last decade of the city's life. In the plinth, with two compartments with plants, panels with stretched garland or carpet edges alternate with squares with corollas or rectangles with opposing palmettes. The central aedicule, rather flat and supported by slender Corinthian columns, has the bottom framed by a trapezoidal carpet border, on which rest, like acroteria, a medallion with a deer and phoenicians; In the center of the aedicule there is a female figure in flight. In correspondence with the alcoves along the E and S walls there is a simple field of tesserae arranged in an oblique warp, while the free part of the antechamber was decorated with an interweaving of horizontal and vertical black bands. The marginal flounce of the room is made up of black tesserae arranged in a straight warp.

Cubicle (43), N wall: the purple plinth has an unusual hexagonal frame in the central panel for a usual sea monster; the side panels, separated by compartments with corollas, are crossed by carpet edges and taut garlands, in large tufts. A stucco frame marked the beginning of the upper black area with a cusped aedicule in the centre, connected by long edges of triangulated carpet to the aedicules at the ends of the wall.

Frigidarium (44): the floor of the room was made up of cocciopesto with rows of large white tesserae, in which was inserted a carpet of 3.65 x 3.11 m of mosaic with black tesserae, arranged in an oblique warp, with flakes of colored marble, including the Numidian and the Holy Bearer, and of green limestone and with the frame of squares with different geometric motifs. Frigidarium (44): the basin leans against the S wall, which was accessed via three external steps and two internal steps covered with painted plaster painted azure, like the entire interior of the basin. Room (45), N wall: the primitive function of this room as a triclinium is attested by the articulation of the decoration of the III style with the central aedicule with a vignette, already in a very poor state of preservation at the time of its discovery, with a woman seated on a cylinder, who touched with her left hand a table suspended from a thin column, surmounted by a vase,  and in his right hand he held a patera; side panels with squares with sacred landscapes. In the upper white area, which in the final arrangement was at eye level, the columns of the central aedicule and a blue band continue.

In the squares of the side panels there were sacred landscapes that were difficult to read. In the upper white area you can see the traces of the gabled tympanum of the central aedicule.

Mau, after describing the vignette with a woman seated on a chair with a backrest, near a cylindrical cist painted in red, towards which he looks, commented "The concept is very graceful, the execution light and decorative, but the conservation not good" (cited in bibl., p. 29, n. 14). The imprint of the frames remains of the side paintings and in the upper area you can still read the tympanum of the central aedicule and the slender side architecture. The marginal flounce is made up of black tesserae arranged in a straight warp.

Tepidarium (46), wall E: the simple decoration of the fourth style has a black plinth, the middle area with red panels separated by architectural glimpses with a yellow background, closed at the bottom by black partitions. A stucco frame with tabs marks the attachment of the lunette, in which a still life with pomegranates was painted, which was interrupted in correspondence with the circular splayed window. Caldarium (47), N wall: the plaster, painted in the fourth style, was applied to the tegulae mammatae from the middle area upwards, as the plinth was made of marble slabs, removed by ancient prospectors. 351. Caldarium(47): in the S wall there is a niche at the flat end with a lowered dome roof, outlined by a stucco frame with lotuses and palmettes. The plinth was covered with marble slabs, the middle area is red and in the upper part there are traces of a carpet border with circumscribed palmettes lying down; the molded stucco frame marks the beginning of the vault.

On a purple background the valve of a large blue shell is outlined, in front of which are a sea griffin and three white-gray dolphins. The stucco frame with lotuses and palmettes was made with a matrix whose ends coincided with the axis of the lotuses.
353. Caldarium (47), S wall, niche: detail of the W section of the cap in which the same motif of the previous figure was repeated, which is less preserved today.
